chapter: Ellington band: drinking, quarrels and rent parties
title: Who Duke left alone: Brown, Tizol and Tricky Sam
summary: Duke liked people who talked back; Lawrence Brown never did and was never close to him, while Tizol and Tricky Sam told him to leave them alone.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: People who gave him a little bit of trouble or talked back he seemed to like better than the people who were -- didn't ever raise their voices.
No, he -- like Lawrence Brown wouldn't say nothing to him, you know.
Well, he and Lawrence weren't close.
No, never close. He didn't bother Tizol. He didn't bother Tricky because Tricky would tell him in his West Indian, 'Leave me alone. Don't bother me. Don't play with me.'
And he wouldn't tell him anything anymore then (unintelligible). And he wouldn't trouble Cootie.
